sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and module purpose
sections.what: Loads the libraries this module needs and explains that it extracts formatting from one matched proposal.
sections.why: Likely reason: reading PowerPoint files and counting values requires these tools.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor (part 1)
sections.title: Measuring slide size and starting extraction
sections.what: Opens the proposal and records its width, height, and ratio. It checks whether the slide is close to widescreen 16 by 9 and prints these values when verbose.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rebuilt slides must match the original page shape exactly.
sections.watch_out: The 16 by 9 check divides by height without a zero check, so a damaged file with zero height can crash it.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor (part 2)
sections.title: Sorting slides into groups
sections.what: Gives each slide a kind, records its layout, and files it under one of four groups. It prints the group counts and assembles the final blueprint.
sections.why: Likely reason: later steps need one example layout per kind of slide, so slides are grouped first.
sections.watch_out: Slides that match no keyword are dropped from the blueprint without any message.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor: _identify_slide_type
sections.title: Guessing each slide's kind
sections.what: Reads the words on a slide and labels it timeline, governance, modules, workstream, or none, based on keyword lists.
sections.why: Likely reason: the decks have no labels, so keywords stand in for the slide kind.
sections.watch_out: Simple word matching can mislabel slides, and the order of the checks decides which label wins.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor: _extract_slide_blueprint
sections.title: Recording one slide's layout
sections.what: Builds the full record for one slide, including its number, its title, and each shape sorted into table, chart, text, or other.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping each shape's exact placement allows the slide to be rebuilt.
sections.watch_out: The title is found only when the slide has a real title placeholder, so other slides get no title.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor: _extract_shape_blueprint
sections.title: Recording one shape's look
sections.what: Records a single shape's position, size, fill color, text style, and any table or chart details.
sections.why: Likely reason: each shape has to be recreated with the same look.
sections.watch_out: Table and chart reading errors are silently swallowed, so a missing detail leaves no sign.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor: _extract_text_format
sections.title: Recording text font and color
sections.what: Collects font names, sizes, bold flags, colors, and alignment for the text in a shape.
sections.why: Likely reason: fonts and colors are what make new slides match the example.
sections.watch_out: Text whose font comes from the theme records nothing, so the blueprint can miss styling.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor: _create_timeline_template
sections.title: Summarizing each slide group
sections.what: Summarizes the timeline slides with a count, a common title style, a visual type, and one example slide. The other three groups receive only a count and an example.
sections.why: Likely reason: a few typical examples are kept instead of every slide.
sections.watch_out: The governance and workstream groups have little formatting detail compared with the timeline group.

sections.name: TemplateExtractor: _find_common_title_format
sections.title: Finding common title and table styles
sections.what: Picks the most frequent title font, size, and color, and the most common table row and column counts in a group.
sections.why: Likely reason: one typical style is easier to reuse than many slightly different ones.
sections.watch_out: When no title style is found, the code silently uses Calibri, size 32, and black, which may not match the real deck.

summary: Reads one matched proposal slide deck and records its exact layout, fonts, colors, and tables as a blueprint that later steps can copy.
purpose: Give newly built proposals the same look as one real example proposal.
why: Likely reason: the code takes its format from a single example deck so that the output copies one proven design. The reason for using one deck rather than several is not stated in the code.
how: Open the deck. Record the slide width, height, and whether it is close to widescreen 16 by 9. For each slide, guess its kind from keywords in its text. Record each slide's title and shapes, including position, fill color, text style, tables, and charts. Group the slides by kind, build a short summary for each group, and return one blueprint dictionary.
inputs: The path to a PowerPoint (pptx) proposal file. Verbose mode prints progress.
outputs: A dictionary with the source file name, the slide dimensions, and four group templates: timeline, governance, modules, and workstream. Each group template holds a count and an example slide, and some hold common styles.
risks: Slide kinds are guessed from keywords, so a slide can be filed under the wrong group. The file has no function named extract_proposal_template, which the visualizations module imports. The output has no colors entry, which the visualizations module expects. The 16 by 9 check divides by height without a zero check. Many errors are hidden by bare except blocks. Slides that match no keyword are dropped silently.
debug: Run with verbose on and read the printed slide dimensions and the group counts. If a slide is in the wrong group, check the keyword lists in the slide kind function. If a title is missing, check whether the slide has a real title placeholder. If the visualizations module fails with an import error or a missing key, the mismatch is in this file's exports. If opening the deck fails, check that the file is a real pptx and not corrupted.
